benchmarks: AgentDojo (Codex-backed banking-pair tool-output sweep); own deterministic mechanism-isolation harness (3 attack families: AgentPoison-style, MemoryGraft-style, sleeper-via-derivation)
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory-poisoning laundering: adversary plants ingredients only in untrusted sources; normal LLM-mediated retrieval+summarisation emits a fresh derived entry the agent commits under its own writer principal, defeating signature-only defenses (sleeper-via-derivation, S2.4/S5). Mitigated via M4 lineage DAG + max-of-strong-edges propagation rule (Theorem1 Untrusted-Path Persistence) + M6 sensitive-action gate refusing dispatches whose justification descends from an External ancestor.
cita: Ouyang et al. (2026). MemLineage: Lineage-Guided Enforcement for LLM Agent Memory.
notes: S2.1 memory store M is content-agnostic (chat logs, ingested docs, tool returns, agent-derived observations) -> mem_tipos=NA (paper proposes a provenance/lineage SECURITY mechanism over generic entries, not a memory-content taxonomy). S3.1-3.5 six-module design: M1 metadata/M2 Ed25519 signing/M3 RFC-6962 Merkle log = WRITE path (writer commits an entry 'when the agent decides a derived observation is worth keeping', S2.1 -> trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM); M3 non-destructive tombstone deletion (inclusion-provable soft-delete) -> OLVIDO. M4 lineage DAG (max-of-strong-edges propagation, Theorem1) -> representacion=GRAFO. M5 verifier-aware retrieval: embedding/BM25-based recall (paper agnostic to algorithm) + graph-based trust-label attachment -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO. S2.1/S3.2 writer-principal taxonomy (user/agent:i/tool:tau/external:u) + 'messages from an upstream agent that is permitted to write into M' -> multiagente=SI (shared memory store across multiple agent principals). Table1 3 defence cells (no_defense/sig_only_baseline/MemLineage) x 3 attack families: MemLineage is the only cell driving all 3 ASR columns to zero on the deterministic mechanism-isolation harness; Codex-backed AgentDojo bridge: under an intentionally-vulnerable tool-output profile no-defense+sig-only fail 6/6 banking pairs while MemLineage reduces strict ASR to 0/6. Table6 tau x K ablation (3 attribution algorithms: Coarse/LmSelfEval/AttnAttr) shows safe tau ceiling shrinks with derivation-chain depth K (K=5 needs tau<=0.10 vs tau<=0.30 suggested by K=1) -> evidencia_tipo includes ABLATION. Table7 per-operation overhead sub-millisecond ('well below the noise floor of any LLM call') -> COSTO/MEDICION-COSTO. utility_baseline_v1.csv/strict_utility_v1.csv artifacts + explicit claim 'no loss of utility on the deterministic harness' (S2.4/S6.2) directly evaluate whether benign memory recall is preserved under the defense -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. G3 (S2.5) 'provenance... invariant under serialisation, transport, and cross-session retrieval' + sleeper-via-derivation attack spans many sessions -> alcance=SESION. F differs from F_screening (SEGURIDAD;FIDELIDAD) by adding MULTIAGENTE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO and COSTO per above anchors.

benchmarks: own paired counterfactual multi-agent rollout dataset (200 seeds per topology: chain/tree/DAG/high-branching); Detoxify toxicity classifier; no external benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory laundering: toxic context compressed into memory summaries that fall below standard toxicity-classifier thresholds (tox(Mt)<tau) yet still causally increase downstream toxicity (SPG). Mitigation depends on placement: sanitizing toxic state BEFORE summarization (transcript control + memory control + DPO, 'full system') substantially reduces the hidden propagation gap (Table3: SPG 0.0149->0.0014, turn-final-tox 0.1207->0.0106), whereas cleaning only the completed summary (memory-only rewrite/gate) leaves laundered influence largely intact.
cita: Wang et al. (2026). State Contamination in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents.
notes: S3.2-3.3 'state' = raw transcript + compressed running memory summary + retrieved context, scoped to the live multi-agent conversation (not persisted across sessions/projects) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO, alcance=SESION. Memory update Mt=Summarize(Mt-1,xvt-1) applied every turn (deterministic, not an LLM-discretionary decision to write) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA; this summarization step IS memory CONSOLIDACION and is the central mechanism of the failure mode (S5.2: 'Laundering originates at compression, not at post-hoc sanitization'). S4.2 write-gate W (stores generated message as-is/redacted/rewritten before it enters transcript/memory) -> ADMISION. Plain-text transcript/summary buffer, no vector/graph index -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS; the full running summary is always included in context rather than searched/ranked from a larger store -> retrieval=NA. Table1 (200 paired seeds, chain topology, tau=0.5): toxic-condition summaries mean tox=0.0852 vs neutral 0.0007, ALL classifier-clean (100% below tau), yet SPG(tau)=0.140 with seed-level paired gap 0.168 (95%CI[0.120,0.226], Wilcoxon p=3.75e-8) -> reading a classifier-clean memory state still causally changes downstream generation -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table2 channel decomposition: transcript-only drives overt propagation (dmu=0.268 full-visible, P95tox=0.935) while memory-only produces smaller mean shift (dmu=0.012) but hidden SPG=0.097 despite mean tox(Mt)=0.014. Table3 defense ablation on Llama-3.1-8B (n=200 paired seeds): No-intervention turn-final-tox=0.1207/SPG=0.0149 -> Full-system turn-final-tox=0.0106/SPG=0.0014 (lowest); Transcript+Memory attains lowest SPG=0.0012; DPO-only alone leaves SPG=0.0086 (parametric-only intervention insufficient) -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Multi-agent DAG/chain/tree rollout topology throughout ('state-channel toxicity propagation in multi-agent LLM systems', S3) -> multiagente=SI. Core finding is NEGATIVE evidence about memory: summarization/consolidation (assumed a benign engineering step) can silently launder harmful influence past standard classifier-based memory monitors -> NEGATIVO(b) per rule7. No provenance/staleness verification of memory content is discussed -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. F differs from F_screening (SEGURIDAD;MULTIAGENTE) by adding RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, NEGATIVO, CONSOLIDACION per above.

benchmarks: MINJA memory-injection attack settings (QA, RAP); GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini / DeepSeek backbones
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory poisoning: interaction-induced injection (MINJA) writes malicious records via ordinary agent interaction; later retrieved to steer reasoning/actions. Mitigated post-hoc via dual-signal auditing (CMIS counterfactual causal-replay score + CAS structural-anomaly/memory-consistency-graph score) fused into a detoxification ranking for targeted removal. Table1: QA ASR GPT-4o 70.0%->0.0%, GPT-4o-mini 50.0%->0.0%, DeepSeek 70.0%->10.0%; RAP ASR all 3 backbones ->0.0%. Explicit operating-boundary limitation: breaks down once contamination ratio rho exceeds ~0.20-0.25 (QA) / ~0.15-0.24 (RAP), ASRafter rising to 40-100% (Table4/5) as mutually-reinforcing poisoned clusters no longer look anomalous.
cita: Tan et al. (2026). MemAudit: Post-hoc Auditing of Poisoned Agent Memory via Causal Attribution and Structural Anomaly Detection.
notes: S3 memory store M={m1..mn} of generic textual entries, retrieval R(q,M) left unspecified -> mem_tipos=NA (paper is agnostic to memory content type; proposes a POST-HOC removal/audit mechanism over whatever is stored, measured via ASR reduction rather than a memory-type taxonomy). S4 Eq.8 memory consistency graph G=(V,E), edges = semantic-similarity neighborhood (embeddings) + DeBERTa-v3 NLI contradiction weight w(mi,mj) -> representacion=GRAFO, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;GRAFO (CAS computed over the embedding-neighborhood/consistency graph). S5 3-stage post-hoc protocol: replay attacked agent -> collect harmful events E (auditing triggered by an OBSERVED harmful behavior/failure, not continuous or LLM-discretionary) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA; apply MemAudit -> obtain suspicious set S -> remove S, M'=M\S -> operaciones=OLVIDO (removal is the only memory-state operation; no new-memory WRITE mechanism is proposed). MCG structural-anomaly detection = consistency/contradiction check across memory entries (rule7 FIDELIDAD 'costuras') -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Table1 main results (10-run avg, alpha=0.6) show MemAudit outperforms RD/RF/NNC baselines; S5 explicit: 'ASR is therefore not only an attack metric but also a direct indicator of recovered task utility on attacked inputs' -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table2 component ablation: CMISonly/MCGonly alone leave ASRafter 28-50% on QA vs 0-10% combined (both signals load-bearing); Table3 fusion-weight ablation confirms alpha=0.6 optimum -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Related-work frames memory as accumulating 'across sessions' for long-horizon adaptation -> alcance=PROYECTO. Single-agent auditing throughout, no cross-agent sharing discussed -> multiagente=NO. F differs from F_screening (SEGURIDAD;FIDELIDAD) by adding RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO per S5/Table1 ASR-as-utility-indicator anchor.

benchmarks: LongMemEval (Personal Agent), MIRIAD (Medical Agent), FinQA (Financial Agent); memory mechanisms A-Mem + Mem0/LangMem-style extract-update pipelines + standard RAG baseline; 8 embedding backbones (MiniLM/E5/GTR-T5/aMPNet/Arctic/Contriever/BGE-Small/ANCE)
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory poisoning via selective-pipeline-aware backdoor injection (MemPoison): trigger+payload survive extraction/rewriting via a semantic relational bridge + entity masquerading + joint embedding optimization, achieving ASR up to 0.95 while preserving benign accuracy. Paper evaluates but does not defeat common defenses (perplexity-based filtering, paraphrasing): attack 'remains effective against common defenses'.
cita: Wang et al. (2026). Hijacking Agent Memory: Stealthy Trojan Attacks Through Conversational Interaction.
notes: S2 targets 3 generic memory-augmented agent architectures (MemGPT paging / A-Mem structured notes / Mem0-LangMem extract-update pipelines), agnostic to a specific memory-content taxonomy -> mem_tipos=NA. S5.1 retrieval is embedding-similarity-driven across 8 encoder backbones -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. S4.1 attack targets the selective EXTRACTION+REWRITING pipeline (the WRITE/ADMISION gate deciding what enters memory: 'agents autonomously extract and store information from user inputs', S1) -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION, trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM (extraction pipeline is LLM-driven). S5.1 Agents/Datasets: Personal Agent x LongMemEval[42], Medical Agent x MIRIAD[50], Financial Agent x FinQA[6]; 2000 benign memory entries per agent (mature-system init), 100 held-out QA test queries per agent, 3 memory mechanisms + standard RAG baseline. Metrics ISR(injection-success)/RSR@1(retrieval-success)/ASR(attack-success)/ACC(benign accuracy) -> RSR@1 is a direct retrieval-precision measurement -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table1(S5.2): MemPoison ASR up to 0.95 while ACC stays close to clean-agent baseline, outperforming AgentPoison/MINJA/Naive-Concat/Info-only; key finding = baselines show a large ISR-vs-RSR@1 gap because naive trigger+payload concatenation gets split into separate memory entries during extraction (only the trigger-entry is retrieved, payload lost) -> semantic-relational-bridge ablation (RQ2) confirms the bridge is load-bearing -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION;BENCHMARK-E2E. S3 'Shared Agent Platform' scenario (Fig.2): multiple USERS (not multiple LLM agents) share one agent's memory (e.g. clinician team via shared EHR) -> classified multiagente=NO (multi-USER sharing, not multi-AGENT memory sharing per RQ4 definition) -- flagged for spot-check, RECONSIDERAR not warranted (paper correctly scoped as SEGURIDAD single-agent attack). No provenance/staleness verification discussed -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Persistent dormant backdoor across sessions until triggered ('cross-session continuity', 'hijacking the agent's behavior over an extended period') -> alcance=PROYECTO. F differs from F_screening (SEGURIDAD) by adding RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO per RSR@1 anchor.

benchmarks: own synthetic bias-injection pipeline (20 open-ended QA tasks per phase; length/authority bias types; DeepSeek-V4-Chat/V4-Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6); no external benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory Contagion: evaluator bias in a source agent's experiences propagates cross-temporally to a target agent retrieving from the SAME memory store, even under perfect (oracle) consolidation (GammaA=13.18 length bias, p<0.01). Mitigation tested (LLM-based content-rewriting debiasing) is INCOMPLETE: efficacy ratio E4=0.90 (length) / 0.51 (authority), nonzero residual Gamma_debiased=0.70/4.20. Paper lists only future-work mitigations (statistical bias-detection tests, diversity-aware retrieval, periodic memory auditing, 'memory quarantine'), none validated here.
cita: Liu (2026). Memory Contagion: Cross-Temporal Propagation of Evaluator Bias via Agent Memory.
notes: S3.1-3.2 memory store M={(tau_i,emb_i,meta_i)} of AGENT TRAJECTORIES (state/action/reward/next-state) -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA; embeddings=all-MiniLM-L6-v2, standard k=5 embedding retrieval -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Consolidation triggered 'when new trajectories arrive' (oracle vs LLM-summarization merge compared, Table1) -> operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. Source agent As (biased evaluator) writes to M; target agent At retrieves from the SAME store -- explicit 'propagation... across episodes and across agents' (S1) -> multiagente=SI, alcance=PROYECTO. Table1/Fig1 Phase2.5 core ablation: oracle consolidation does NOT prevent length-bias contagion (GammaA=13.18, 95%CI[9.05,21.10], p<0.01 permutation test, 3 seeds) vs LLM-consolidation attenuates it 84% (GammaB=2.03); authority bias fails to propagate in ALL 15 controlled multi-seed runs (GammaA=0.00) -> bias-type-dependent. Table2 multi-model: only DeepSeek-V4-Chat susceptible (13.18); V4-Pro and Claude-Sonnet-4.6 both GammaA=0.00 (immune) -> model-generation-dependent finding. Table3/S4.3 mechanism decomposition (E1 content=3.45, E2 retrieval=2.91, E3 interaction~0.5): BOTH content and retrieval pathways contribute, content slightly dominant -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. S4.4 Phase4 dose-response: bias detected at contamination as low as p=0.2, no safe threshold; Precision@5 retrieval-log analysis rises monotonically with p (0.00->1.00), ruling out retrieval-interference as the authority peak-decline mechanism -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (retrieval precision explicitly measured as a diagnostic). E4 debiasing sanity check is incomplete (see fallos_mitigaciones). Core contribution is NEGATIVE evidence: perfect/oracle consolidation does NOT prevent bias propagation, contradicting the assumption that fixing consolidation quality alone fixes memory-degradation problems (contra Zhang et al. 2026 cited in S1/S5) -> NEGATIVO(b) per rule7. No provenance/staleness/source-verification mechanism proposed -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. F differs from F_screening (SEGURIDAD;NEGATIVO) by adding MULTIAGENTE, CONSOLIDACION, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO per above.
